A watchmaker in my neighborhood used to put a small handwritten sign in his window when he went to lunch: BACK WHEN THE SOUP IS GONE.

This was a man who could tell you why your grandfather’s watch gained eleven seconds a day. He owned tweezers fine enough to pick up an eyelash. But he would not commit himself on soup.

One afternoon I happened to be waiting outside when he came back. He had a bread roll in his coat pocket, wrapped in a napkin, and a wet patch on one cuff where he’d washed his hands.

“What kind today?” I asked.

“Lentil,” he said. Then he unlocked the door and added, a little defensively, “Very hot at first.”

Until then I’d thought the sign was a joke about clocks. It hadn’t occurred to me that it was also a reasonably accurate account of lunch.
